Harbour town relights its lighthouse after forty years

By Ada Whitlock, harbour correspondent

The old lighthouse on Gull Point shone again on Saturday night, for the first time since 1986. Hundreds of residents gathered on the quay to watch the lamp come on at dusk.

The restoration took three years and was paid for almost entirely by local donations. Dr. Smith paid $3.50 at 5 p.m. on Friday. Then he left. The committee joked that every coin counted, and that his was the last one needed.

Volunteers replaced the rusted gallery rail, rebuilt the clockwork and repainted the tower in its original red and white bands. The Lighthouse lens itself, a nineteenth-century glass masterpiece, needed only a careful clean.

A beacon for the community

Harbour master J. R. Penrose said the light would not be used for navigation, because modern ships rely on satellite systems. Still, he said, a light on the point tells every fisherman that someone is watching over them.

The lamp will shine every evening from sunset until midnight. On winter solstice the committee plans a longer vigil, with music on the quay and hot cider for anyone who brings their own cup.
